title: Personal Injury Intake and Cases
description: For injury lawyers: intakes, limitations dates, records, liens, offers and net to client.

spec.useCase: Nadia Petrov is a case manager at a personal injury firm and uses this to return new intakes in a day, chase medical records requests and see which signed cases are ready for a demand. Operational tracking only; it holds no legal advice.

text.text: Your personal injury practice in one place. Start with Intakes to call today, track each signed Case through its stages, and keep Records requests and Offers moving. Operational tracking only; strategy and privileged notes stay in the case file.
Injured people call several firms. The firm that calls back fast, listens and explains clearly is the one they sign with. Good screening also protects the firm from cases it cannot win.
Within one hour of the inquiry
Add the intake with name, source, incident type and
Call back. Leave a voicemail and send a text if they do not answer; try again in two hours.
The date sets the limitations clock.
Police report number, witnesses, photos, video.
ER, urgent care, primary doctor, specialists. Gaps in treatment hurt claims.
: the at-fault party's carrier, the client's own auto policy (medical payments and uninsured motorist coverage), health insurance.
Has the client given a recorded statement or signed anything for an insurer?
Advise them not to until you are retained.
Any prior injuries to the same body part?

Kenji was rear-ended at a light 15 days ago and is seeing an orthopedist. He signed after a 20-minute call; letters went to Pellston Mutual and his own carrier the same afternoon.
Every case moves through the same stages. Knowing what finishes each stage keeps cases from sitting for months without progress.

text.text: Photos of the scene, injuries and property damage saved
Witnesses contacted while memories are fresh
Video requested from businesses before it is overwritten (often within 30 days)
Case managers check in with the client every two weeks: appointments kept, new providers, how they are feeling.
Every new provider gets a records request row straight away.
The demand package tells the story: liability, injuries, treatment, bills, lost wages, how life changed, and a specific number.
when treatment ends. Aim to send within 30 days of the last record arriving.
Negotiation ends with an accepted offer or a written decision to file suit. Do not let a case sit in Negotiation for more than 60 days without that decision.
Once suit is filed, court deadlines are tracked as their own dates and the case manager keeps the client informed of each step.
Every Monday, filter cases with a limitations date in the next 180 days that are not resolved. For each, the attorney decides by 90 days out: settle or file.
Call every client at least once a month at every stage, even when nothing changed. Silence is the top complaint injured clients have about their lawyers.
Niall's case is at Records and bills with his therapy records chased two days ago. Once they arrive, the demand target date this week can hold.
The demand is only as strong as the records behind it, and records are the slowest part of most cases. A steady weekly chase shortens every case.
Add a row for each provider: ER, ambulance, imaging, specialists, therapy, pharmacy.
Send a signed authorization with a request for complete records and an itemized bill. Ask for billing codes on the bill.

cells.text: Call the records department; confirm they received it
Second request in writing; mark Chased
Ask the client to call their provider; offer a records service if the firm uses one

text.text: Note every call on the request's page.
Records complete for the dates of treatment
Itemized bill received and amount entered in
Pages indexed so the attorney can find key findings quickly
Health insurers, government programs and some providers will claim repayment from the settlement. Ask every client who paid their bills, and send lien inquiry letters early.
on the case as letters come back. Final lien amounts are negotiated after settlement.

Lost wages need proof too: a letter from the employer with dates missed and pay rate, and pay stubs from before the injury. Self-employed clients need tax returns. Add these as their own request rows.
Keep copies of every request letter and authorization on the case.
Kenji's orthopedic records were due for follow-up yesterday. The case manager calls the practice today, learns the request went to the wrong office, and resends it.
A records request with no follow-up date is a request nobody is watching.
on each case. A case cannot move to Demand while it is above zero, unless the attorney decides to send without a provider.
Every offer is logged, explained to the client in writing with the net amount, and answered in a reasonable time. The client decides; the firm advises.
Work out the net: fee, costs advanced, liens.
Net to client at best offer
shows it for the highest offer.
Call the client the same day. Follow with an email or letter showing the offer, the net and the attorney's advice.
Record the client's decision and respond to the carrier: Countered, Rejected or Accepted.
Compare the offer with verdicts and settlements for similar injuries in your area.
Consider policy limits: an offer at limits may be the most the carrier can pay; ask about other coverage, such as the client's own underinsured motorist policy.
Be plain about the time and risk of going to trial.
Counter with a specific number and a short reason (new records, future treatment, lost wages). Avoid tiny moves; they signal the end of your range.
Release reviewed by the attorney before the client signs
Settlement check deposited in the trust account
Settlement statement signed by the client showing fee, costs, liens and net

Lucia's third offer came in 30 days ago after two counters. The net at that offer is shown on the case. The attorney recommends mediation, the client agrees in writing, and the response is set to Countered.

When negotiation stalls, mediation often settles the case. Send the mediator a short statement with the key records, and prepare the client for a long day and a final number they are comfortable with.
Never accept or reject an offer without the client's decision in writing.
Never disburse before the settlement statement is signed.

The case desk of a personal injury practice: calls from injured people, every case with its limitations date, the medical records and bills that build the claim, and the offers that end it. Pleadings and medical files stay in your document system.
